Topical ciclosporin, in strengths ranging from 0.05 to 2% has been shown to be effective1,2 in the treatment of various ocular surface disorders, particularly dry eye (see be- low) and atopic keratoconjunctivitis. It has also been used for corneal ulcers, glaucoma (see below), as adjunctive therapy in corneal allograft rejection, and for the ocular manifestations of graft-versus-host disease. A silicone matrix ocular implant that provides sustained release of ciclosporin (LX-201) is under investigation for the prevention of rejection in corneal transplantation. 1. Tatlipinar S, Akpek EK.
